subject: phys
source: Cambridge IGCSE Physics (0625) syllabus for examination in 2026, 2027 and 2028 — Cambridge International; Year 10 covers topics 1–3 and the start of topic 4 (first half of the two-year course)

weeks.topic: Physical quantities and measurement techniques; scalars and vectors
objectives: Measure length, volume and time using appropriate instruments
Distinguish scalar and vector quantities
Find a resultant of two perpendicular vectors

weeks.topic: Motion: speed, velocity and acceleration
objectives: Calculate speed and average speed
Define velocity and acceleration
Use a = Δv/Δt

weeks.topic: Distance–time and speed–time graphs
objectives: Sketch and interpret distance–time and speed–time graphs
Calculate distance from the area under a speed–time graph
Describe free fall and terminal velocity

weeks.topic: Mass, weight and gravitational field strength
objectives: Distinguish between mass and weight
Use W = mg
Describe gravitational field strength

weeks.topic: Density: measurement and flotation
objectives: Calculate density using ρ = m/V
Measure density of regular and irregular solids and liquids
Predict whether objects float

weeks.topic: Effects of forces: resultant force, F = ma and friction
objectives: Find the resultant of forces in a line
Apply F = ma
Describe friction and drag as forces opposing motion

weeks.topic: Hooke's law and load–extension graphs
objectives: Plot and interpret load–extension graphs
Define the spring constant and limit of proportionality
Describe circular motion as needing a perpendicular force

weeks.topic: Turning effect of forces: moments and equilibrium
objectives: Define the moment of a force
Apply the principle of moments
State the conditions for equilibrium

weeks.topic: Centre of gravity and stability
objectives: Describe how to find the centre of gravity of a plane lamina
Explain how the position of the centre of gravity affects stability

weeks.topic: Momentum and impulse
objectives: Define momentum and impulse
Apply conservation of momentum to collisions
Relate resultant force to rate of change of momentum

weeks.topic: Energy stores and transfers; conservation of energy
objectives: Identify energy stores and transfer pathways
Apply the principle of conservation of energy
Draw Sankey diagrams

weeks.topic: Kinetic and gravitational potential energy; efficiency
objectives: Use Ek = ½mv² and ΔEp = mgΔh
Calculate efficiency of energy transfers

weeks.topic: Work and power
objectives: Define work done as force × distance moved
Define power as rate of energy transfer
Calculate power using P = W/t

weeks.topic: Energy resources: renewable and non-renewable
objectives: Describe how electricity is generated from fossil fuels, nuclear, wind, hydroelectric, solar and geothermal sources
Compare their advantages and disadvantages
Explain the Sun as the source of most energy resources

weeks.topic: Review: motion, forces, momentum and energy
objectives: Practise motion graph and equation questions
Revise energy calculations and resources

weeks.topic: Pressure in solids and liquids
objectives: Use p = F/A
Calculate liquid pressure using Δp = ρgΔh
Explain applications of high and low pressure

weeks.topic: Kinetic particle model: states of matter and Brownian motion
objectives: Describe the particle arrangement in solids, liquids and gases
Explain Brownian motion as evidence for particles

weeks.topic: Gas pressure, temperature and absolute zero
objectives: Explain gas pressure in terms of particle collisions
Relate temperature to average kinetic energy and absolute zero
Use pV = constant at constant temperature

weeks.topic: Thermal expansion of solids, liquids and gases
objectives: Describe thermal expansion and its relative order in solids, liquids and gases
Give everyday applications and consequences

weeks.topic: Specific heat capacity
objectives: Define specific heat capacity
Use ΔE = mcΔθ
Describe an experiment to measure specific heat capacity

weeks.topic: Melting, boiling and evaporation; specific latent heat
objectives: Describe melting and boiling at constant temperature
Explain cooling by evaporation
Distinguish boiling and evaporation

weeks.topic: Conduction and convection
objectives: Explain conduction in solids including free electrons in metals
Explain convection currents in liquids and gases
Investigate good and bad thermal conductors

weeks.topic: Thermal radiation and consequences of thermal energy transfer
objectives: Describe infrared radiation and the effect of surface colour and texture
Explain everyday applications such as vacuum flasks and radiators

weeks.topic: General properties of waves: transverse and longitudinal
objectives: Describe wavefronts and wave motion
Define amplitude, wavelength, frequency and period
Compare transverse and longitudinal waves

weeks.topic: The wave equation and wave behaviour: reflection, refraction and diffraction
objectives: Use v = fλ
Describe reflection, refraction and diffraction using a ripple tank
Explain how gap size affects diffraction

weeks.topic: Reflection of light and plane mirrors
objectives: State the law of reflection
Construct ray diagrams for plane mirrors
Describe the virtual image formed

weeks.topic: Mid-year exams: motion, forces, energy and thermal physics
objectives: Complete timed papers on content taught so far
Show full working in calculation questions

weeks.topic: Refraction of light: refractive index, critical angle and total internal reflection
objectives: Use n = sin i / sin r
Define critical angle and describe total internal reflection
Explain optical fibres

weeks.topic: Thin lenses: converging and diverging lenses and ray diagrams
objectives: Define focal length and principal focus
Draw ray diagrams for converging lenses
Describe lenses used to correct sight

weeks.topic: Dispersion of light and the visible spectrum
objectives: Describe the dispersion of white light by a prism
Recall the order of the colours of the visible spectrum
Define monochromatic light

weeks.topic: The electromagnetic spectrum: properties and uses
objectives: State the order of the electromagnetic spectrum
Recall that all EM waves travel at the same speed in a vacuum
Describe uses of each region

weeks.topic: Hazards of EM radiation and digital communication
objectives: Describe harmful effects of EM radiation
Compare analogue and digital signals
Explain uses of microwaves and radio in communication

weeks.topic: Sound: production, speed, echoes, pitch and loudness
objectives: Describe sound as longitudinal waves needing a medium
Measure the speed of sound in air
Relate pitch to frequency and loudness to amplitude

weeks.topic: Ultrasound and its uses
objectives: Define ultrasound and the human hearing range
Describe uses in medical scanning and sonar

weeks.topic: Simple phenomena of magnetism: magnets and magnetic fields
objectives: Describe forces between magnetic poles
Distinguish magnetic and non-magnetic materials
Plot magnetic field lines with a compass

weeks.topic: End-of-year exams: motion, forces, energy, thermal physics and waves
objectives: Complete end-of-year papers on all Year 10 content
Apply physics to unfamiliar contexts

weeks.topic: Review: thermal physics, waves, light and sound
objectives: Correct errors from end-of-year exams
Consolidate equations and ray diagrams before Year 11
